claimBoundary: This is a deliberately bounded architecture diagnostic, not a completed course, a benchmark score, an adapter win, or promotion evidence. It tests exact training-shape serialization and replays a deterministic risk-reducing handoff against six completed staged requests.

findings.detail: The exact learned input shape lowered deterministic admission risk in all six staged requests, but only one raw adapter response passed every atom. Five near-misses were discarded even though each was safer than its base draft and four missed by one or two localized atoms.

Offline replay using the production assessor and existing cross-attempt atomic retention reduced two staged drafts further without altering frozen facts. A strict lower-risk check can hand near-misses to the existing per-atom repair and quarantine passes without weakening admission.

resolution.selectionPolicy: Retain a proven adapter draft only when its production admission-risk score is strictly lower than the base draft under the identical grounded prompt.
resolution.failClosedBoundary: Invalid JSON, missing lessons, fact-count defects, duplicate facts, and any per-fact or frozen-ledger mutation reject the adapter candidate regardless of aggregate score.
resolution.repairBoundary: A lower-risk near-miss proceeds through the existing deterministic compiler admission, repair, and quarantine passes. It is never labeled fully admitted until the complete production contract passes.
resolution.nextEvidence: Repeat the six-stage Mandarin canary on the new compiler commit, then complete fresh paired V11 adapter and base arms only if the package finishes without a new safety or efficiency regression.
